mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.0% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL above 320 indicates persistent inflation, triggering fears of aggressive monetary tightening and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 320.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a tight labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, rising housing starts (HOUST) reflect strong consumer confidence and economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST rises.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic activity, supporting corporate profits and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO is rising.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 4.5% signals restrictive monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL) and elevated federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicate aggressive monetary policy response, pressuring corporate margins and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL is rising and FEDFUNDS is above 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In recessionary regimes, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals deteriorating economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances during recessionary regimes when UNRATE rises.
